title: Fan-out and Aggregation: The Gateway as a Composer — Check

questions.prompt: What is the primary job of the Agronomy Studio gateway?
questions.explanation: The gateway composes: it calls several domain services concurrently and assembles their results into one coherent response for the client.
options: To store all agronomy data in a single database
To fan out to multiple domain services and compose one response
To render the Blazor UI on the server
To replace the domain microservices entirely

questions.prompt: Using `Promise.all` to fan out to three services makes the client wait roughly for the slowest service rather than the sum of all three.
questions.explanation: `Promise.all` runs the calls concurrently, so total time is bounded by the slowest call, not the sum.

questions.prompt: Why is server-side composition usually faster than letting the browser call every service directly?
questions.explanation: A single client round trip plus fast intra-region fan-out beats many slow client-to-third-party round trips.
options: Server-to-server calls within a region avoid many high-latency client round trips
The gateway caches every possible response forever
